prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: A library shelf at the end of an aisle with two small glowing figures of mist: a river-shaped ripple and a veiled bride; the ink-stained spirit sweeping its pen over them so that their outlines ripple like water; Dādī pointing and explaining.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
kavika: A small blue-black spirit with ink-stained wisps, a reed pen behind one ear.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
MANDATORY TEXT OVERRIDE: this card authorizes NO writing in the painting. Where the scene brief or character description mentions letters, a register, script, writing, numbers, sacred symbols or letter-shaped objects, show the corresponding physical door, pillar, book, leaf, crown or cord WITHOUT any letters or letterlike marks. Use purely floral carvings and completely blank smooth manuscript surfaces. Teaching letters remain separate live app text. No typography, numerals, Om signs, invented script, explanatory marks, sound lines, watermark or labels anywhere.

image.brief: A library shelf at the end of an aisle with two small glowing figures of mist: a river-shaped ripple and a veiled bride; the ink-stained spirit sweeping its pen over them so that their outlines ripple like water; Dādī pointing and explaining.

alt.en: Two glowing mist figures, a river and a bride, on a library shelf as a poet-spirit sweeps his pen over them
alt.hi: पुस्तकालय की अलमारी पर दो चमकते धुंध-आकार: नदी और वधू

narration.en: At the end of the aisle, two words stand side by side on a shelf: a river and a bride, both long vowels, both feminine. The poet spirit sweeps his pen over them, and their endings ripple like water. “The long ones,” says Dādī. “Words in -ई and -ऊ. Feminines, mostly. They do what the short ones do, with a different rhythm.”
narration.hi: गलियारे के छोर पर अलमारी पर दो शब्द साथ-साथ खड़े हैं: एक नदी और एक वधू, दोनों दीर्घ स्वर, दोनों स्त्रीलिंग। कवि-भूत उन पर कलम फेरता है, और उनके प्रत्यय पानी की तरह लहराते हैं। “दीर्घ वाले,” दादी कहती हैं। “-ई और -ऊ वाले शब्द। अधिकतर स्त्रीलिंग। वे वही करते हैं जो ह्रस्व वाले, अलग लय में।”

body.en: Feminines in long -{{ई}} ({{नदी}}, {{देवी}}, {{कन्यका}}-like {{गौरी}}) and -{{ऊ}} ({{वधू}}, {{भू}}) share a pattern. Before a vowel-initial ending the long vowel becomes {{य्}} or {{व्}}: {{नद्यौ}}, {{वध्वौ}}. Sūtra 4.1.5 makes many of these feminines with {{ङीप्}}.
body.hi: दीर्घ -{{ई}} ({{नदी}}, {{देवी}}, {{गौरी}}) और -{{ऊ}} ({{वधू}}, {{भू}}) वाले स्त्रीलिंग एक ढाँचे पर चलते हैं। स्वर से शुरू होने वाले प्रत्यय से पहले दीर्घ स्वर {{य्}} या {{व्}} बन जाता है: {{नद्यौ}}, {{वध्वौ}}। सूत्र 4.1.5 इनमें से कई स्त्रीलिंग {{ङीप्}} से बनाता है।

caption.en: A river, in every case and number
caption.hi: नदी, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: The call is short: {{हे नदि}}. {{नद्याः}} serves both the fifth and the sixth singular.
note.hi: पुकार छोटी है: {{हे नदि}}। {{नद्याः}} एकवचन पञ्चमी और षष्ठी दोनों का काम करता है।

caption.en: A bride, in every case and number
caption.hi: वधू, हर विभक्ति और वचन में

note.en: The {{ऊ}} turns to {{व्}} before vowels: {{वध्वौ}}, {{वध्वाः}}. The call is {{हे वधु}}.

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the table.

explain.en: Every form is in the table you just read.
explain.hi: हर रूप उसी तालिका में है जो अभी पढ़ी।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of a feminine in -ऊ.
prompt.hi: -ऊ वाले एक स्त्रीलिंग के छूटे रूप भरिए।

explain.hi: {{वधू}} उसी ढाँचे पर {{व्}} के साथ चलती है।

prompt.en: Join each form to its case.
prompt.hi: हर रूप को उसकी विभक्ति से जोड़िए।

explain.hi: स्वर से पहले {{ई}} {{य्}} बन जाता है।

prompt.en: Tap every form of {{नदी}} that has {{य्}}.
prompt.hi: {{नदी}} के हर रूप को छुइए जिसमें {{य्}} है।

success.en: “वध्वः,” you say, and the little veiled bride on the shelf lifts her veil and laughs. The river-ripple beside her unfolds, unfolds, and runs the length of the aisle in a silver line.
success.hi: “वध्वः,” आप कहते हैं, और अलमारी की नन्ही घूँघट वाली वधू घूँघट उठाकर हँस पड़ती है। उसके पास की नदी-लहर खुलती है, खुलती है, और गलियारे की पूरी लम्बाई में चाँदी की रेखा बनकर बह जाती है।

failure.en: The bride stays veiled. The plural of {{वधू}} is {{वध्वः}}.
failure.hi: वधू घूँघट में रहती है। {{वधू}} का बहुवचन {{वध्वः}} है।
